Description

Two membrane proteins hold parts of the cascade at internal membranes. Sef binds active MEK, prevents the MEK:ERK complex from dissociating and blocks the nuclear translocation of active ERK. ERK held by Sef still phosphorylates RSK2 in the cytoplasm but no longer phosphorylates the nuclear transcription factor Elk-1, so Sef directs the signal to cytoplasmic targets [1]. Sef has been placed at the Golgi, and it also serves ERK activated by RAS at the endoplasmic reticulum [2, 3]. RKTG (PAQR3), an integral protein of the Golgi, binds RAF1 and moves it from the cytoplasm to the Golgi. This blocks the move of RAF1 to the plasma membrane after EGF and its phosphorylation on Ser338, and reduces its interaction with RAS and MEK1 [2].
